title: Ankhorage Infra
summary: Plans, generates, applies, inspects, and destroys project infrastructure through independently released provider adapters.
purpose: Provide one project-aware infrastructure lifecycle while keeping cloud, cluster, storage, database, and policy technologies replaceable behind explicit adapters.
responsibilities: Resolve project and environment infrastructure specifications into deterministic plans.
Coordinate validation, generation, lifecycle operations, outputs, credentials, and stored infrastructure state.
Expose the infrastructure capability through a standalone library, CLI, and Ankh runtime provider.
boundaries: Does not implement provider-specific cloud, cluster, database, storage, or policy operations inside the core lifecycle.
Does not own application deployment or secret-store provider implementations.
Does not assume a particular hosting topology; concrete behavior is selected through declared adapters.
audience: Application teams planning and operating independently deployable project infrastructure.
Infrastructure adapter authors integrating supported technologies with the canonical lifecycle.
useCases: Validate and plan an application's infrastructure for a selected environment.
Generate or reconcile infrastructure through released provider adapters.
Inspect outputs and status, or explicitly destroy environment-owned resources.

architecture.role: Infrastructure application and composition owner over portable contracts and replaceable provider adapters.
invariants: Environment lifecycle policy depends on portable contracts rather than concrete provider SDKs.
Provider implementations are resolved through published adapter packages and validated descriptors.
Destructive lifecycle operations remain explicit and environment-scoped.

configuration: Operations require an application manifest, explicit environment selection, and configuration for each selected provider.
security: Provider credentials and destructive confirmation remain explicit boundary inputs rather than embedded metadata.
